# Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic delivers full keyboard operability for the four audited core Dashboard
flows — project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run
submission — as enumerated in the accessibility audit. When complete, each flow
can be completed end-to-end with keyboard alone: focus is managed correctly
through modals and dialogs, no control is unreachable, and visible focus
indicators render consistently across the audited surfaces.

## Scope

- Remediate the per-flow keyboard defects enumerated in the accessibility audit
  for the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission):
  - Eliminate focus loss and focus traps in modal and dialog interactions.
  - Make all controls in the audited flows keyboard-reachable and operable.
- Apply consistent, visible focus indicators across the audited flows' controls,
  following the Dashboard's existing component patterns.
- Cover HLR-1 (keyboard operability, no focus traps or unreachable controls)
  and HLR-2 (consistent visible focus indicators).

Out of scope per the strategy: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard
fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the project creation flow, When the user completes it using keyboard
  input only, Then every step is operable, focus remains managed (no loss, no
  traps), and no control is unreachable.
- Given the workbench spawn flow, When completed with keyboard only, Then every
  step is operable with managed focus and no unreachable controls.
- Given the model deployment flow, When completed with keyboard only, Then every
  step is operable with managed focus and no unreachable controls.
- Given the pipeline run submission flow, When completed with keyboard only,
  Then every step is operable with managed focus and no unreachable controls.
- Given the controls across the four audited flows, When any receives keyboard
  focus, Then a visible focus indicator is rendered consistently with the
  Dashboard's focus-indicator pattern.
- Measured by: each of the four flows passes a keyboard-only walkthrough aligned
  with the audit's per-flow defect list (all enumerated defects resolved).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with
  no focus traps or unreachable controls.
- HLR-2 (P1): Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows.

documentation required by the two public-sector customers before renewal: the
VPAT (conformance statement) and the product documentation accessibility
statement, rewritten to reflect the fixed state of the four audited Dashboard
flows and republished through the Red Hat docs content process.

  operability and focus-indicator state of the four audited core flows
  (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run
  submission).
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement accordingly.
- Republish both artifacts through the documentation content pipeline.

- Given the completed keyboard accessibility remediation of the four audited
  flows, When the VPAT is updated, Then it accurately reflects the fixed
  conformance state of those flows.
- Given the updated VPAT, When the product docs accessibility statement is
  revised, Then it is consistent with the VPAT's claims.

  four flows before publication (doc review against implementation, per the
  docs-authoring contract).
- Both artifacts are republished and publicly available.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P2): The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed
  state, with technical review.
